requirement.original: Move ALL session recovery responsibility into the happy daemon TypeScript codebase. Kill the bash watcher entirely. The systemd service files should also be generated/managed by happy itself (either daemon or CLI), not manually maintained. The user has '强迫症' — ownership must be clean and unambiguous.
requirement.clarified: Implement daemon-owned session recovery: (1) Daemon persists session snapshots to disk on every lifecycle event + periodic safety writes, (2) Daemon restores sessions from snapshot on startup, (3) Daemon generates/installs its own systemd service files via 'happy daemon install', (4) Remove all external recovery infrastructure (bash watcher, ExecStartPre/ExecStartPost, post-start script).
requirement.what: Move session recovery from bash scripts into daemon TypeScript code; add systemd service file generation to CLI
requirement.why: Clean ownership — 5 components with tangled responsibilities caused production incidents (Bug #60, #61). User wants single source of truth for session lifecycle.

included: Startup recovery (read snapshot, spawn sessions with --resume)
Shutdown snapshot (write before exit in cleanupAndShutdown)
systemd service file generation (happy daemon install/uninstall for Linux)
PID file self-management (daemon writes its own daemon.pid)
Orphan cleanup on startup (already partially exists)
Atomic file writes for snapshot (write-to-temp + rename)
excluded: Remote restore triggers from mobile app
Backward compatibility with bash watcher protocol
macOS LaunchDaemon changes (keep existing mac/install.ts as-is)

success_criteria: Daemon writes session_snapshot.json on every session add/remove/crash event
Daemon writes final snapshot in cleanupAndShutdown before exit
Daemon reads snapshot on startup and restores sessions with --resume
Periodic safety writes happen every 60s via heartbeat
happy daemon install generates correct systemd service file for Linux
happy daemon uninstall removes service file and reloads systemd
Generated service files have NO ExecStartPre, NO ExecStartPost
All 4 existing daemon services can be regenerated with correct parameters
Corrupted/missing snapshot file does not crash daemon startup
constraints: Must use atomic writes (temp file + rename) for snapshot to prevent partial reads
Restore must stagger session spawns with 5-second delays
Each daemon scoped to its own HAPPY_HOME_DIR — no cross-daemon state
Dev daemon uses different binary path (/usr/bin/happy-dev) — service template must support this
Cannot use 'happy' global CLI binary from within daemon (CLAUDE.md rule #9)
Must not use kill PIDs directly — use existing process management patterns (CLAUDE.md rule #10)

root_cause_analysis.symptom: Session recovery spread across 5 components with unclear ownership, causing cross-daemon cascade (Bug #61) and race conditions (Bug #60)
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: Recovery was designed incrementally: bash script first, then systemd hooks layered on, then daemon crash respawn added separately. No single component owned the full lifecycle.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause_commit: N/A - architectural debt accumulated over multiple commits
root_cause_analysis.why_introduced: Each piece solved an immediate need: bash script for manual recovery, systemd hooks for automatic restart, daemon respawn for crash resilience. Never unified.
root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: 5 components with overlapping responsibility: (1) bash watcher snapshots vs daemon tracking, (2) ExecStartPre saving vs daemon shutdown write, (3) ExecStartPost restoring vs daemon startup restore, (4) watcher auto-restore vs daemon crash respawn. Cross-daemon cascade in Bug #61 was direct result of global restore scope.
root_cause_analysis.timeline: Accumulated over weeks of incremental additions, incidents on 2026-04-04 and 2026-04-05

research_findings.reason: Straightforward architectural consolidation — moving existing bash logic into existing TypeScript daemon. Patterns are well-established in the codebase (atomic writes in persistence.ts, spawn with --resume in run.ts, heartbeat loop for periodic tasks). No novel design patterns needed.

context.codebase_state: Daemon already has: pidToTrackedSession tracking, onChildExited with crash respawn, spawnSession with resumeSessionId support, heartbeat loop for periodic tasks, cleanupAndShutdown for graceful exit. Missing: snapshot persistence to disk, startup restore from snapshot, systemd service generation for Linux.

development_approach.strategy: Implement in 4 phases: (1) Add snapshot types and persistence functions, (2) Wire snapshot writes into daemon lifecycle events, (3) Add startup restore logic, (4) Implement systemd service generation. Each phase is independently testable.

phase_1_types_and_persistence.description: Add SessionSnapshotEntry and SessionSnapshot interfaces to types.ts. Add sessionSnapshotFile path to configuration.ts.

session_snapshot_entry.happySessionId: string | undefined — happy server session ID

session_snapshot.daemonPid: number — PID of daemon that wrote this

phase_2_snapshot_writes.description: Add writeSessionSnapshot() helper in run.ts. Call it from: (1) after successful session spawn, (2) in onChildExited after removing session, (3) in heartbeat loop, (4) in cleanupAndShutdown before apiMachine.shutdown()
phase_2_snapshot_writes.atomic_write: Write to session_snapshot.json.tmp, then rename to session_snapshot.json
phase_2_snapshot_writes.data_source: Extract from pidToTrackedSession.values() — only include sessions with claudeSessionId AND workingDirectory

phase_3_startup_restore.description: Add restoreSessionsFromSnapshot() function. Call after apiMachine.connect() and before heartbeat loop.
flow: 2. Parse and validate (skip on error with warning log)
3. For each entry: verify .jsonl file exists at expected path
4. Spawn with 5-second stagger: await spawnSession({ directory, resumeSessionId: claudeSessionId })
5. Log results: N restored, M skipped (missing .jsonl), K failed
phase_3_startup_restore.error_handling: Each session restore is independent; one failure does not abort others

phase_4_systemd_install.description: Create linux/install.ts with service file template. Update install.ts to dispatch on platform.

service_template_params.name: string — e.g., 'jade', 'dev', 'qijie' or empty for default

ExecStartPost lines from all 4 daemon services
